name: Salem
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Salem, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Salem, MA: Santa on the Hawthorne Hotel roof, the Lappin Park tree, Santa at the Common, a Christmas Carol trolley and PEM crafts.
lede: In December, Salem turns to Holiday Happenings: Santa lands on the roof of the Hawthorne Hotel, a lantern procession leads to the tree at Lappin Park, and families add Santa at the Common, trolley theater and ornament making at PEM.
celebrates: Salem's season begins when Santa arrives at the top of the Hawthorne Hotel with help from the Salem Fire Department, then leads a lantern procession down the Essex Street Pedestrian Mall to the Holiday Tree at Lappin Park, next to the Bewitched statue. Salem Main Streets and the Creative Collective run Salem Holiday Happenings through December. Historic Salem Inc. opens decorated homes for its Christmas in Salem tour on the first weekend of December, the city's recreation department brings Santa to the Salem Common Gazebo, the Salem Trolley stages A Christmas Carol on board, and the Peabody Essex Museum runs drop-in art making for families.
lastyear: In 2025 Santa arrived at the Hawthorne Hotel on Friday, November 28, and led the procession to the tree lighting at Lappin Park, according to Destination Salem. The 46th annual Christmas in Salem house tour followed on December 6 and 7, a holiday window decorating contest began downtown on December 7, and Wassail Weekend on December 13 and 14 brought roaming carolers and Santa appearances on the Sunday. Chabad of Beverly-Salem lit a grand menorah at Lappin Park on December 20.
facts: Christmas was once against the law in this part of Massachusetts. In 1659 the Massachusetts Bay Colony passed a law called Penalty for Keeping Christmas, which fined anyone caught celebrating by skipping work or feasting five shillings, about $48 today. The colony repealed the ban in 1681. Today Salem's Holiday Tree is almost always donated by a Salem resident with an overgrown tree, and Historic Salem Inc. says its Christmas in Salem tour inaugurates the holiday season with a new neighborhood and theme each year.
trains: Salem station is on the MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line, with trains to North Station in Boston, and the Peabody Essex Museum is about half a mile away by Washington Street and the Essex Street pedestrian walkway. The MBTA has added extra weekend trains for Salem's Haunted Happenings in October. Farther afield, Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train through the lights, and Lowell has the National Streetcar Museum and the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society's steam locomotive No. 410.

kidfact: Long ago, celebrating Christmas was against the rules in Salem's colony. From 1659 to 1681, anyone who skipped work or held a feast on Christmas could be fined five shillings.
faq: Where does Santa arrive in Salem?

Santa arrives at the top of the Hawthorne Hotel at 18 Washington Square West, with help from the Salem Fire Department, on the Friday after Thanksgiving. Salem Main Streets recommends reaching Salem Common by 5:45 pm. Santa then leads a procession down the Essex Street Pedestrian Mall to the Holiday Tree Lighting at Lappin Park, and families are invited to carry lanterns.

It is a holiday house tour run by Historic Salem Inc. on the first weekend of December, with a candlelight preview the Friday before. Homeowners open decorated historic houses to thousands of visitors, and each year features a different neighborhood and theme. Tickets are sold through Historic Salem Inc., and the tour is held on the first weekend of December.
Is there a Christmas Carol show in Salem?

Yes. Salem Trolley and The Gallows Hill Theatre present a humorous, interactive A Christmas Carol on board the Salem Trolley from late November until just before Christmas. Each show lasts 1 hour 15 minutes and leaves from Timeless Life Treasures on Wharf Street. Shows sell out quickly, so book on FareHarbor.
Is the Peabody Essex Museum free for kids?

Yes. PEM admits youth under 16 free, and Salem residents also get in free. Adults pay $25, seniors $23 and students with ID $15. December weekend art making, such as paper ornaments in the Create Space Studios, is included with admission, and the museum is open 10 am to 5 pm Thursday through Monday.
How do I get to Salem by train?

Take the MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line from North Station in Boston to Salem station. From the station, follow the path up to Bridge Street, then walk down Washington Street to the Essex Street pedestrian walkway. The Peabody Essex Museum is about half a mile from the station on that route.
